recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any future heading or grammar polish should be treated as editorial only; no semantic FHIR-48702 follow-up is needed in core source.
issue_request: FHIR-48702 asked that pipe characters used as canonical version delimiters in HTTP GET search examples be percent-encoded. The Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution instead approved a near-top note explaining that examples are shown unescaped for readability, with actual over-the-wire URL encoding still required.
initial_application: Source commit d83729a5d4743f1218b4e53aad9e70c5363880da applied the issue to source/search.html by adding Notes on URL-Encoding, updating example selectors to say Show as unencoded, linking pipe-delimited syntaxes to the note, and preserving encoded examples only where encoding is discussed. Jira comment history says HL7/fhir#3442 was merged.
additional_context: The linked Zulip conformance thread confirms that the pipe remains the delimiter and should not be replaced with ?version, but it must be escaped in actual HTTP. The 2025-03-17 FHIR-I minutes record a 16-0-0 motion to add the explanatory note and keep readable examples unescaped.
reconciliation: No source change was necessary. Current source/search.html already contains the approved URL-encoding note, the unencoded and encoded over-the-wire examples, and links from canonical/reference and token syntaxes that introduce pipe-delimited forms.
